scope: Structural adequacy screen of an existing beam-telescope regression fixture; no comparative-benefit or physical-calibration experiment
prior_inspection: Source code, example documentation, table schemas, row counts and stored fit arguments were inspected. Event rows, hit/miss counts and selected-sample outcomes have not been read before this protocol and its executable are frozen. Original authors have already analyzed the data. This is retrospective research, not preregistration before measurement.
checks: For every DUT table, report rows, unique events, multi-row events, monotonicity, bit-pattern counts, finite track fits and missing evaluated-DUT hits.
Independently compare all six hit bits with finite x/y coordinates and positive n_hits fields; retain discrepancies if present.

For DUT3, fixed from the upstream efficiency test before reading outcomes, report all saved rows and a reference-quality subset requiring hits and quality bits for DUTs 0,1,2,4,5 and track_chi2 < 15. Do not require DUT3 hit, quality or isolation bits.

Report the two chronological halves of unique event IDs descriptively, without fitting, tuning or declaring a held-out calibration pass. Neither half remains blinded after this screen. No ROI or efficiency target is selected.
adequacy_gate: At least one saved track without a hit on the evaluated detector is necessary to demonstrate that misses are retained; this alone is insufficient for a valid efficiency denominator.

Resolve upstream detector-dependent association, trigger and alignment selection before calling a reference independent. The default candidate finder can use all DUTs even when the final fit excludes one.
Trace this exact fixture to its physical run and processing chain; a related example's Run36 description is not sufficient by itself.

A later beam-efficiency or fluence decision requires a separate physical bridge, matched established tag-and-probe/Kalman baselines, costs and an improvement gate before evaluation. Beam coordinates do not validate Lorentz chronology.
delivery: Publish the small protocol, executable and descriptive result with source identities; keep downloaded public source bytes in an external cache. Do not redistribute the HDF5 fixture or equate the software MIT license with a verified independent data license. No Lean invocation is part of this screen.
